note: The Python modules js/layer_a.js, js/image_meta.js, js/av_meta.js, js/container_meta.js, js/stylometry.js and js/gumbel.js were ported from the upstream sources listed below. Some sources are tracked one definition or one range of definitions at a time rather than whole-file, through `slice`: container_meta.py and common.py are mostly filesystem, ZIP, PDF and subprocess plumbing that has no browser counterpart, and an issue that is usually noise is an issue nobody reads. scripts/check-upstream.mjs compares the live content against these hashes. The parity suite proves the ported behaviour still matches for the cases it covers; this catches the rest: new options, new formats, anything the fixtures do not exercise. When one moves, re-port it and update `sha256` in the same commit.
followUp: If the parity suite is still green, the change is probably additive: a new format or option the fixtures do not reach. Add fixtures covering it, or the gap stays invisible the next time too.

sources.comment: Deliberately partial: upstream #156 hardened the error handling around the external c2patool subprocess (a failed run is inconclusive, not 'no C2PA'). There is no c2patool and no run_optional_tools in a browser, so js/image_meta.js has nothing to mirror there. Partial for the same reason since upstream 8e16b822, which passes creationflags=subprocess_creationflags to every subprocess.run so a child process opens no console window on Windows: a browser starts no child processes. Everything else in this file is ported. Partial in two more ways since 2026-08-27: upstream #252 refuses HTTP redirects in _synthid_score_http to block SSRF, and #254 adds a `changed` field to clean_image's returned dict for clean_file.py's new --only-changed flag. Neither has a browser counterpart: this port makes no HTTP calls, and clean() returns bytes rather than writing a file, so the caller already holds both sides to compare. Partial in one more way since upstream #261, which turns clean_image's post-clean scan into a residual scan: it adds an include_exiftool toggle to run_optional_tools/inspect_image, reuses synthid_before when no pixel remover ran, and lets inspect_image take pre-read bytes. A browser starts no exiftool subprocess, runs no SynthID scorer, and inspect() already takes bytes. Upstream #264 is ported in full: the C2PA ContentProvenanceBox user type d8fec3d6-1b0e-483c-9297-5828877ec481 is recognized and stripped in inspectIsobmff and stripIsobmff, so AVIF/HEIC and, through js/av_meta.js, MP4/MOV now lose a manifest whose payload carries no ASCII c2pa/jumb marker. Upstream #308 is ported in full: a zTXt/iTXt value that inflates past MAX_PNG_TEXT_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES (1 MiB) is refused rather than allocated, inspectPng reports the chunk as not fully inspected and stripPng drops it even in keep mode. The same commit swapped zlib.decompress for a decompressobj, so a stream that stops early now yields the prefix it decoded instead of nothing; js/image_meta.js's own inflate does the same, and keeps returning null for a stream that is corrupt rather than merely short. Partial in three more ways since 2026-09-01. #302 renamed the CtrlRegen and DiffusionPurification `strength` parameters to `intensity`: those are subprocess flags for pixel-domain removers a page cannot run. #201 added synthid_is_watermarked and made inspect_image report the SynthID verdict as a finding, which needs the scorer this port does not have. And run_synthid_score and _synthid_score_http gained a `data` parameter to skip a read-back, which is meaningless where inspect() is handed the bytes to begin with.

This port used to diverge here: upstream's _strip_moov_udta rebuilt an MP4 from the boxes that parsed and dropped everything after them, so a truncated download lost its media while the action list still said the tail was kept. Reported as guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover#240 and fixed upstream by #242, which keeps the tail the same way and adds an inspection_incomplete flag that clean_av folds into still_has_ai_metadata. js/av_meta.js carries the same flag as inspectionIncomplete through both drivers, and tests/test_av_meta_parity.py now asserts the two agree. Partial in the same way image_meta.py is: inspect_av and clean_av take filesystem paths and use safe_write_bytes, which has no counterpart in a browser. clean_av's post-clean re-inspection is also not mirrored: the page inspects before cleaning and reports through the UI instead. Partial in one more way since upstream #254: clean_av's returned dict gained a `changed` field for clean_file.py's new --only-changed flag. cleanAv here returns the bytes rather than writing a file, so the caller already holds both sides to compare. Upstream #201 is ported in full: an ID3v2 tag whose declared size overruns the file is reported as truncated instead of silently parsing to nothing, and a clean drops it up to the first valid MPEG frame header, or preserves the file when there is no such header to find. js/av_meta.js carries it through both drivers, and the slice driver scans for the frame header in chunks rather than reading the file. Partial in one more way since the same commit's neighbour: inspect_av gained a `data` parameter so an HTTP caller can skip the read-back, which a page that already holds the bytes has no use for.

Ported in full apart from the command-line surface: print_human_stylometry_report and main() have no counterpart in a page, and score() returns the to_dict shape directly. Since upstream #258 a sample below MIN_SAMPLE_WORDS reports score and confidence_level as null rather than 0.0/CLEAN, and every report carries density_tier; matched markers carry spans as code-point offsets, which is why js/stylometry.js maps UTF-16 string indices back to code points before recording them.

Tracked as one definition, not as a file. classify_finding_confidence is the only thing js/stylometry.js mirrors from common.py, because StylometryReport.to_dict() calls it; the rest of common.py is filesystem and subprocess plumbing with no browser counterpart (read_text_input, backup_path, safe_write_bytes, the tool probes). Hashing the whole file would open a drift issue every time upstream touched any of that, and an issue that is usually noise is an issue nobody reads. Added after upstream #273 changed this function, classifying Layer A space homoglyphs as informational, and nothing here noticed.

AI_FRONTMATTER_KEYS, AI_META_NAME_RE, GENERATOR_NAME_KEYS, AI_FREE_TEXT_MARKER_RE and named_value_is_ai. Tracked as a range of definitions rather than as a file: container_meta.py is 4,000 lines and most of it is ZIP and PDF work built on zipfile, tempfiles and external tools, with no browser counterpart, so hashing the whole file would open a drift issue every time any of that moved. This is the rule upstream #336 and #342 settled: a value names a generator only under one of GENERATOR_NAME_KEYS, where it is matched against image_meta's AI_GENERATOR_PRODUCTS; every other name carries free prose and is matched only against markers that are never ordinary English.

_blob_hits and the embedded data-URI scanner (_iter_data_uris, _skip_data_uri_candidate, _inspect_embedded_data_uris, _clean_embedded_data_uris), ported in full. Upstream #306 rewrote these from regexes into linear character scans to remove a polynomial ReDoS; the reasoning holds here for a different reason, since what it stalls in a browser is the tab rather than a single-process service. An image inside a data: URI is handed to the same strip_png/strip_jpeg/strip_webp/strip_isobmff this port already mirrors.
_iter_tag_blocks, _drop_tag_blocks and _drop_blocks_if: the linear pairing of opening and closing tags that replaced the lazy '.*?</close>' idiom, preserving its match semantics.

The whole SVG section: the block regexes, inspect_svg, the XML declaration scanners from upstream #288 (_xml_decl_keyword, _xml_decl_end, _strip_xml_declarations), _strip_root_svg_attrs and clean_svg. Ported in full. Note the two decode modes, which are not interchangeable: clean_svg uses surrogateescape so a file that is not valid UTF-8 survives byte for byte, while inspect_svg uses replace. js/container_meta.js writes both out by hand, because TextDecoder offers neither.

_FM_RE, _parse_simple_yaml_keys, inspect_markdown and clean_markdown, ported in full. The nested-block rule matters more than it looks: dropping an AI key has to drop the indented lines under it, or `model:` goes and `name: claude-opus` stays.

The whole HTML section: _meta_attrs, _is_cms_generator_meta, _meta_tag_is_ai, _find_tag_end, _iter_script_blocks, _script_tag_is_jsonld, inspect_html and clean_html. Ported in full, with one deliberate divergence, which is the second one this port carries after the truncated-MP4 fix that upstream later took as #242. _iter_script_blocks and _iter_data_uris lowercase the whole document to find '<script' and 'data:image/', then index the ORIGINAL string with the result's offsets. That holds only while lowercasing preserves length, and U+0130 does not: it lowercases to two characters in Python and in JavaScript alike, so every offset after it is off by one. One such character earlier in a file hides a JSON-LD provenance block from upstream's inspect AND its clean, and mis-parses an embedded data URI into a different MIME type and a truncated payload. js/container_meta.js lowercases ASCII only, which cannot change length. tests/test_container_meta_parity.py asserts the divergence in both directions, so it fails loudly if upstream fixes this and the two converge again.
